caps: Every year, | in homes across India,
lines.tts: Every year, in homes across India, a tulsi plant becomes a bride. And her groom... is a stone.

caps: And the first wedding | of the season... | is *HIS.*
lines.tts: For four months, Lord Vishnu sleeps. On देवउठनी Ekadashi, he wakes. And the first wedding of the season... is his.
But who is she? The Devi Bhaagvatam says, she was a princess, Tulasi, born on Kartik Poornima.

caps: For a *LAKH* divine years | she did *TAPASYA,*
lines.tts: For a lakh divine years, she did tapasya, with one wish: Naaraayan, as her husband.
Brahma told her: first, you will marry another. Afterwards, you will have Naaraayan.
She married शंखचूड़, a mighty daanav king. While her vow stayed unbroken, death could not touch him. He took heaven from the gods.
Shiva went to war against him. And Vishnu went to Tulasi's palace... in her husband's form.
Tulasi's vow was broken. On the battlefield, Shiva's trishool struck.

caps: Then she saw | who he *REALLY* was.
lines.tts: Then she saw who he really was. Your heart is like stone, she cried. So become a stone!

caps: He said: | you did tapasya | for *ME.*
lines.tts: Vishnu accepted her curse. He said: you did tapasya for me. Now you will have me, forever.

caps: Your body will flow | as the *GANDAKI* river.
Your hair will grow | as the holy *TULSI.*
And I will lie | on your bank, | as stone:
lines.tts: Your body will flow as the Gandaki river. Your hair will grow as the holy tulsi. And I will lie on your bank, as stone: the Shaaligraam.
Her curse... and her prayer... came true, together.

caps: That's why | a *SHALIGRAM* | is never worshipped
lines.tts: That's why a Shaaligraam is never worshipped without tulsi. And every Kartik, when Vishnu wakes, we marry them.

caps: give her away, | as their own | *KANYADAAN.*
lines.tts: A mandap in the courtyard. A red chunari for the bride. Families with no daughter give her away, as their own कन्यादान.

caps: Which name did | *YOU* grow up with?
lines.tts: Other Puraanas call her Vrinda. Which name did you grow up with? Comment, Vrinda, or Tulsi!
